prompt:
Extract a SysML v2 model from the document as a list of facts. Each fact has unit_id (the sentence it comes from), type and slots. Give only the slots that have a value, as a list of {slot, value} pairs; for composition give one 'parts' pair per part.

Types and slots:
  attribute(owner,name,value,unit) action(performer,label) state(owner,label) constraint(subject,expression) requirement(subject,text)
  composition(whole,parts) flow(source,target,payload) succession(before,after) transition(from,to,trigger) allocation(action,to)

Name each element by its full name as first introduced in the document.
RULES:
- Resolve every entity-valued slot using all the text you are given. If a sentence refers to an element by an alias, abbreviation, pronoun or shorter description, write the element's full name as first introduced. If a sentence says an element receives or uses an item and the text you are given states which element produces or sends that item, emit a flow from that producer to the receiver. If an element cannot be determined from the text you are given, use null; never guess.
- Never write placeholder words such as "any", "all", "some state" for an unstated element; use null.
- Do not merge differently named things unless the text says they are the same.
- Emit one action for EVERY behavior verb phrase, including passive voice (performer null), capability statements, displays, logs, generates and reports. label = the verbatim verb phrase with its object.
- Emit a requirement for every NORMATIVE statement (shall, must, should, will, is required to, needs to). Purpose, goal or benefit sentences are not requirements.
- Emit a state for every named mode or state; transitions use the state names, with from null when the prior state is not stated.
- Emit a succession only for an EXPLICIT temporal connective between two actions ("then", "after", "once", "before", "when ... is complete", "next", "finally"); before/after are the action labels. Never use succession for cause or data transfer.
- Resolve a pronoun or "this/these" performer to the element named in the preceding sentence and write that element's name; if it cannot be resolved, use null. Never output a pronoun as a slot value.
- Drop determiners and quantifiers from element names ("Each Soil Moisture Probe" -> "Soil Moisture Probe", "the system" -> "system").
- allocation.to must be a component or actor, never a mode or state.
- Emit a constraint for every threshold, limit, period or deadline stated with a number; expression = the verbatim phrase.
- Emit a flow for every sentence in which an element sends, transmits, reports, displays, commands or delivers an item (target null if the receiver is not named).
 Also list under "entities" every system element, actor or item named in the document units, with its full name and any alias the text explicitly declares for it (e.g. 'hereafter X', 'known as X', 'called X'); aliases [] if none. Return JSON {"entities": [...], "facts": [...]}.

Document units:
U0051: For each condition, they then determine the medical capabilities that are needed as interventions (e.g., prevention, diagnosis, treatment, and long-term management) for the conditions.
U0052: MedOps passes this information to OCHMO.
U0053: OCHMO uses this information to help clarify the level of care definitions and overall capabilities for the DRMs that they had previously defined.
U0054: SCENARIO 2: MASS AND VOLUME ALLOCATION Stakeholders: Exploration Program Systems Engineering Team Life Cycle Phase: Pre-Phase A A DRM for an upcoming exploration mission has just been defined.
U0055: To aid in mission planning, the Exploration Program Systems Engineering Team wants to understand the medical risks associated with the mass and volume allocations for the mission’s medical system.
U0056: One of the Program Systems Engineers asks the IMPACT POC to run several analyses with various mass and volume targets and create curves plotting mass and volume against specific risk metrics, including LOCL, QTL, and RTDC.
U0057: This information helps them determine how raising or lowering the mass/volume allocation affects crew health risks.
U0058: SCENARIO 3: RESEARCH PRIORITIZATION Stakeholders: ExMC Leadership Life Cycle Phase: Pre-Phase A ExMC Leadership has limited funding to invest in research and technology development for future long- duration deep space missions.
U0059: ExMC has received three proposals: 1) a new countermeasure that reduces the occurrence of Spaceflight Associated Neuro-ocular Syndrome by 50%, 2) a new intervention that promises to reduce the likelihood of LOCL due to sepsis by 50%, or 3) a new ultrasound that occupies 25% of the footprint of the existing ultrasound machine.
U0060: ExMC has prioritized the LOCL and QTL factors equally but is less interested in reducing RTDC likelihood.
U0061: ExMC Leadership delivers this information to the IMPACT POC and requests a risk assessment report that shows what happens if the promised reductions in the research proposals fall short of their stated goals.
U0062: The IMPACT POC retrieves the proposed set of available medical capabilities and resources from the medical resource tool and the corresponding medical evidence from the medical evidence tool.
U0063: Using a guided user interface, the IMPACT POC creates new evidence and resource files with the stated reduction goals from the research proposals, as well as additional points at one-third and two-thirds of the stated reduction goals.
U0064: The IMPACT POC runs the scenarios through IMPACT and delivers visualizations of risk reduction for each of the scenarios at each level of goal accomplishment.
U0065: The IMPACT POC also delivers an assessment of figures of merit, such as the operating and storage environmental requirements, shelf lives, and additional vehicle interfaces required.
U0066: This report is delivered to ExMC Leadership, who then prioritizes the three proposals based on the quantitative results.
U0067: SCENARIO 4: RISK ASSESSMENTS Stakeholders: HRP Elements Life Cycle Phase: Pre-Phase A The standards for CO2 levels are being updated for an upcoming long-duration deep space mission.
U0068: There is a debate among the SMEs in various areas of expertise regarding the maximum acceptable level of CO2 exposure for the crew.
U0069: The factors being debated are a risk of higher occurrence of medical conditions, the ability of the crew to properly exercise, the impact on cognitive function and behavior, and the impact on the sensorimotor functioning of the crew.
U0070: An IMPACT POC is asked to provide a risk assessment of elevated CO2 levels from a medical, crew health, behavioral/cognitive, and sensorimotor perspective.
U0071: Each of these correspond to HRP elements, whose SMEs will need to supply the following to the IMPACT POC: 1) an evidence base that details occurrence of certain undesirable states that affect crew health or performance, as well as how variations in CO2 level affect this evidence, 2) a set of risk metrics that quantify effects on crew health, performance or mission success, 3) a list of resources that prevent or mitigate these undesirable states, 4) evidence that ties the availability of these resources to the duration, intensity, time course and/or consequence of these undesirable states, and 5) a tailored version of the probabilistic risk assessment tool that supports the desired output metrics (not necessarily unique to each Element).
U0072: The IMPACT POC is also asked to consider proposed research that modifies the Environmental Control and Life Support System (ECLSS).
U0073: This research may have an effect on the individual resource allocations to preserve overall mission allocation and acceptable risk targets.
